title: Parmesan and Pistachio Olive Oil Popcorn
intro: Bringing Mediterranean ingredients to a movie-night classic turns a simple whole grain into a savory, fiber-rich snack. Popping the corn in olive oil and tossing it with crushed pistachios delivers a satisfying crunch that supports steady blood sugar.

ingredients.name: Shelled pistachios
ingredients.canonical_name: Nuts, pistachio nuts, dry roasted, without salt added

instructions: Heat the extra-virgin olive oil in a large pot with a tight-fitting lid over medium-high heat. Drop in the test popcorn kernels.
Add the remaining popcorn kernels when the test kernels pop. Cover the pot and remove from the heat for 30 seconds to equalize the temperature.
Return the pot to medium heat.
Shake the pot continuously as the corn pops for 2 to 4 minutes. Check the progress at 2 minutes, and stop shaking when the popping slows to one pop every 2 to 3 seconds.
Remove the pot from the heat immediately. Add the chopped pistachios, grated parmesan cheese, garlic powder, dried thyme, and black pepper directly into the hot pot.
Toss the mixture well so the residual heat warms the nuts and helps the cheese stick.
Transfer the popcorn to a large bowl and serve warm.
variation: Trade the dried thyme for a pinch of smoked paprika.
conservation: Best enjoyed right away; does not keep.

[cooking_method_suitability] Tossing dry spices and grated cheese directly onto hot, essentially dry popped corn (since the 2 tsp of oil is absorbed during popping) means the flavorings will fall to the bottom of the bowl. Fix: Add an instruction to lightly mist the popped corn with olive oil spray (or drizzle a tiny bit of reserved oil) immediately before tossing so the cheese and spices stick.

[chapter_intent_fit] The recipe slightly overshoots three strict snack-tier ceilings: saturated fat (2.9g vs 2.0g ceiling), carbohydrates (25.2g vs 24g ceiling), and calories (255 vs 230 ceiling). Fix: Reduce the popcorn kernels from 1/4 cup to 3 tablespoons, and reduce the Parmesan cheese from 3 tablespoons to 1.5 or 2 tablespoons to bring all three values into compliance.
